en.title: HBO's Harry Potter: 5 Characters Who Deserve More Magic
en.summary: With HBO's expansive take on the Wizarding World on the horizon, attention turns to who might step out of the shadows. These five characters could shine brighter in the new series.
en.body:
The upcoming **HBO** adaptation of **Harry Potter** promises a deep dive into J.K. Rowling's beloved books, with an extended runtime per season offering the chance to explore the Wizarding World in unprecedented detail. While the core trio of **Harry**, **Ron**, and **Hermione** will undoubtedly take center stage, portrayed by newcomers **Dominic McLaughlin**, **Alastair Stout**, and **Arabella Stanton**, the true magic of this new series could lie in its development of the wider cast. The films, by necessity, condensed complex narratives, leaving some fascinating characters with limited screen time. This new format is the perfect vehicle to expand their stories.

With a cast that includes esteemed actors like **John Lithgow** as **Albus Dumbledore**, **Janet McTeer** as **Minerva McGonagall**, and **Paapa Essiedu** as **Severus Snape**, the potential for richer character arcs is immense. We're particularly excited about the prospect of seeing more of characters who, in the movies, were often relegated to brief but memorable appearances. Think of the sheer gravitas **Nicholas Hoult** could bring to **Gilderoy Lockhart**, allowing for a more nuanced exploration of his vanity and eventual downfall. Or the potential for **Katherine Parkinson** as **Molly Weasley** to showcase the fierce maternal protectiveness that defines her beyond just the Battle of Hogwarts. Even characters like **Quirinus Quirrell**, listed in a guest/recurring capacity with **Luke Thallon** taking the role, could be given more psychological depth, hinting at his inner turmoil and susceptibility to Voldemort's influence much earlier.

## Unlocking Deeper Wizarding Lore

Beyond the obvious choices, there are other figures whose journeys could be significantly enhanced. Consider **Argus Filch**, played by **Paul Whitehouse**. His bitterness and dedication to the minutiae of Hogwarts' rules often served as comic relief, but a more developed arc could explore the roots of his resentment and his surprising loyalty to the school. His perspective as a Squib offers a unique lens through which to view the magical world. Similarly, **Johnny Flynn** as **Lucius Malfoy** has the opportunity to portray the slippery, self-serving nature of the Malfoy patriarch with more than just sneers and pronouncements. We could see the political machinations and the fear that truly drives his actions, making him a more compelling antagonist throughout the series.

## The Fan Appeal of Deeper Cuts

For the legions of dedicated **Harry Potter** fans who have devoured the books multiple times, these expanded roles are precisely what they've been hoping for. The movies gave us the broad strokes, but the HBO series can now fill in the intricate details that make the Wizarding World so captivating. Giving characters like **Gilderoy Lockhart** or **Argus Filch** more time to breathe allows for a richer tapestry of storytelling, exploring themes of ambition, prejudice, and loyalty from multiple viewpoints. It’s about honoring the depth of the source material and providing satisfying narratives for characters who have long deserved the spotlight.

## What's Next

The **Harry Potter** series is slated for a 2026 release on **HBO** Max. While specific character focus details are still emerging, the extensive cast list and the serialized format strongly suggest that audiences will get to know many more faces of the Wizarding World intimately.

content_raw: HBO's Harry Potter show has more time to dig into the source material. These five overlooked characters deserve more screen time than they got in the movies.
